source: J. S. Lewis (1992), PhD thesis, City University London, Appendix D-2 sample spreadsheet for Test 35A (pp. 267-269)
why_this_run: 35A is the only run whose local Nusselt numbers are printed as numbers rather than plotted. Every other run's local Nu exists only in Figures 6.7-6.13.
the_two_exit_temperatures: 29.32 degC is MEASURED; 30.00 degC is CALCULATED from the corrected power input. The -3.96% energy-balance error is exactly the gap between them. The local-Nu reduction uses the CALCULATED value -- verified by reproducing the printed (Tw-Tb) at x/d=159.33: 59.02 - [13.06 + (30.00-13.06)*(1.8960/1.900)] = 29.06 K, which is the printed value. Using the measured 29.32 gives 29.73 K and does not match.
basis_sensitivity: The property basis moves Re by 24% (1143 -> 1417) and Gr_q by a factor of 2.6. The two are not interchangeable; any matched CFD case must name which it targets.
bulk_temperature_definition: EXPERIMENT: linear rise from the measured inlet (13.06) to the CALCULATED exit (30.00) over the heated length. PREDICTION: Lewis's own code integrates a true mixing-cup bulk (Appendix F, the SUMUCT loop sums U*cp*r*T). These are two different bulk definitions on the two sides of his own comparison.

geometry.note: The 2.5d unheated entry is upstream of x=0 and is where partial hydrodynamic development happens; x/d is measured from the start of heating.
